qolFindings.title: The V7-1 date-shape rule now refuses real telephones written in two-digit groups with dots or dashes, and names them 'not a telephone'
qolFindings.scenario: Probe round8/r8v, readPhone false. Line 'Veldor;Marta;;16;<value>'. '0789.12.34.56', '02-12-34-56', '333-12-34-567', '+39 02.12.34.56.78', '(0789) 12.34.56' and '06/12.34.56' each make the line unread with the reason 'nella colonna Telefono c’è «…», che non è un telefono'. Round 7 ignored all of them, because each has 9 or more digits. The unanchored /\d{1,2}[./-]\d{1,2}[./-]\d{2,4}/ matches inside them. No data is lost: the line is shown with its text and can be fixed in place. But the reason is false, and it contradicts the code comment ('A telephone that was not asked for is ignored, even a malformed one, and never a reason to refuse') and V5F-4 ('a telephone, even malformed, is still ignored'). The prompt tells the assistant to leave the column empty, so this needs an assistant that deviates.
qolFindings.suggestedFix: Anchor the date shape to the whole value, optionally followed by an age: /^\d{1,2}\s*[./-]\s*\d{1,2}\s*[./-]\s*\d{2,4}(?:\s+\d{1,3})?$/. Add '0789.12.34.56' and '02-12-34-56' to the corpus as ignored telephones. Alternatively, reword the comment and V5F-4.

qolFindings.title: V7-1's 'a date written with separators' still overstates: a spaced date with a two-digit year, or six digits, is ignored as a telephone
qolFindings.scenario: Probe r8v, readPhone false. '01 02 10', '3 4 08' and '010210' in the Telefono column give one student with age 16 and no unread line, so the birth date is dropped unseen. '120310' and '12 03 10' are shown only because their digits happen to contain 20xx. V5C-1 says 'a date in the ignored Telefono column is shown as an unread line', and V7-1 says 'a date written with separators … is shown'. Both are true only for dots, slashes, dashes and commas, or a four-digit year. This needs two deviations: the column shifted, and a format the prompt did not ask for. The age is kept.
qolFindings.suggestedFix: Say 'with dots, slashes or dashes, or with a four-digit year'. Or treat a value of 6 digits or fewer made of three 1-2 digit groups separated by spaces as a date.
